content: The George Foundation (TGF) is a non-governmental organization (NGO) founded in 1995, headquartered in Bangalore, India. Its founder, Dr. Abraham M. George, is a successful entrepreneur who returned to India from the United States to initiate various humanitarian projects. TGF's mission is to combat poverty, improve health and environmental conditions, and strengthen democratic values and institutions in India. The organization primarily operates in rural areas of Tamil Nadu, particularly in the Krishnagiri district, and Karnataka, serving over 16,000 individuals across 17 villages. These communities are among the poorest in the country, with over 70% of the population living on less than one dollar per day. Illiteracy and malnutrition rates exceed 60%, and social issues such as female infanticide and bonded labor are prevalent. Alleviation of Poverty TGF's poverty alleviation initiatives focus on enhancing education and healthcare, providing essential amenities like housing and water, and creating sustainable employment opportunities for rural families. Shanti Bhavan Boarding School Shanti Bhavan was established in September 1997 in Baliganapalli, Tamil Nadu, to provide high-quality education to children from impoverished backgrounds. The school began with 48 students and aims to expand to 336 students. Admission criteria prioritize children from the poorest families who demonstrate intellectual potential. The school offers a comprehensive curriculum from preschool to 12th grade, accredited by the Council for the Indian School Certificate Examination in New Delhi. English is the primary medium of instruction, with Hindi and Tamil introduced by the fourth year. Students are also encouraged to engage in extracurricular activities such as sports, art, music, and drama. The campus is designed to be self-sufficient, utilizing solar power, ground wells, water storage tanks, and agricultural resources. Additionally, TGF works to improve the quality of education in local government schools, which often suffer from a lack of teachers and resources. Community Development Program This program targets 17 villages in Tamil Nadu and Karnataka, aiming to significantly improve the quality of life within a decade, starting in 2006. The program encompasses livelihood creation, education, skills training, healthcare, housing, water management, infrastructure development, and social progress. Agri-Business Training Centre and Women’s Empowerment The Women’s Empowerment Project trains women in farming techniques. Participants are provided with land, supplies, and equipment to practice cooperative and cottage farming. As of 2007, this project was still in its preparatory phase. Tillany Fine Arts Museum & Gallery Established in 2000 near Shanti Bhavan, this 15,000-square-foot facility supports underprivileged artists by exposing them to global art, providing tools, and promoting their work. Art sales generate income for the artists, with 40% of proceeds going directly to them. Protection of Health and the Environment Baldev Medical and Community Centre The Baldev Medical and Community Centre serves approximately 30 patients daily across 17 villages in Tamil Nadu and Karnataka. It provides home visits, health checks for children, and health education classes. The center addresses a range of medical issues, including infectious diseases, malnutrition-related conditions, respiratory and gastrointestinal problems, and childbirth complications. Serious cases are referred to city hospitals. The center also organizes annual sanitation drives and offers multi-specialty clinics in areas such as obstetrics, pediatrics, dermatology, and dentistry. Services are provided at minimal cost, based on patients' ability to pay. Lead Poisoning Prevention and Treatment In 1997, TGF launched Project Lead-Free to screen blood lead levels in children, pregnant women, and workers in hazardous occupations. This initiative led to an international conference on lead poisoning in 1999, co-sponsored by organizations such as the World Health Organization and the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. The conference's findings contributed to the Indian government's decision to phase out leaded gasoline by 2000. In 2003, TGF partnered with St. John’s Academy of Health Sciences to establish the National Referral Centre for Lead Poisoning Prevention in India (NRCLPI). Improvement of Governance Indian Institute of Journalism & New Media (IIJNM) Founded in 2001 in collaboration with Sri Adichunchanagiri Mahasamstana, IIJNM offers a curriculum developed with Columbia University’s Graduate School of Journalism. The institute trains students in the craft and ethics of journalism, aiming to strengthen governance through a free and independent press. It is now considered one of India’s top journalism schools. Centres for Studies in Emerging Critical Issues This initiative brings together experts to address economic, social, and environmental challenges in developing nations. The findings are disseminated through papers and lectures. Milestones TGF has significantly improved the economic conditions of the communities it serves. Many individuals, particularly women, now earn stable incomes, enabling them to support their families, access healthcare, and escape bonded labor. Shanti Bhavan has gained international recognition for its achievements, as highlighted in Thomas Friedman’s book The World is Flat. TGF’s support for government schools has increased attendance and academic performance, particularly among girls. The Baldev Medical Centre’s outreach programs have reduced malnutrition, improved sanitation, and decreased maternal mortality rates in the villages it serves. TGF’s efforts to address lead poisoning led to the nationwide adoption of unleaded gasoline in 2000. NRCLPI continues to play a pivotal role in preventing lead poisoning in India. IIJNM has expanded its enrollment and introduced courses in television and radio journalism, earning a reputation as one of India’s leading journalism schools.
